sentences.text: Phocaeicola coprocola is a commensal bacterium whose therapeutic potential was investigated in murine models of Western diet-induced steatotic liver disease and of induced liver fibrosis.
In the Western diet model, administration of this species attenuated hepatic steatosis, reduced lipogenic gene expression and improved metabolic and histological parameters.

In the advanced fibrosis model it significantly reduced cholestatic markers and fibrosis severity, with effects associated with selective downregulation of extracellular matrix-related fibrogenic programs.
Those effects were reported even in the absence of detectable gut colonization, which the authors took to suggest that stable engraftment is not required for therapeutic activity.
In faecal samples from lung cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, Phocaeicola coprocola was enriched in the group that did not develop immune-related adverse events.
